title: A Winter for the Portrait
premise: When Yara Ashgrove returns to the drowned family estate of Ashgrove Hollow to bury his twin sister Ysolde, the body in the casket wears her face but not her memories—and the excavation crew digging a new well unearths a door sealed from the inside, behind which something has been keeping the household's lights burning for a century. The house runs on an inherited song, sung by one Ashgrove per generation to bind the last resident, and Yara learns that his sister died mid-verse, leaving the binding unfinished and the last resident—a woman in a portrait who ages in reverse—desperate to sign the estate over to him before the song ends and she must claim a singer in her place. As winter seals the roads, Yara must learn the song's final verse from his sister's surviving half-memory without ever singing it aloud, choosing between the love he owed his twin and the duty the house demands. In the end he burns the portrait, sings the verse alone as an elegy rather than a contract, and walks out over the ice as Ashgrove Hollow goes dark behind him, finally visible to the world and free of its inheritance.
about_author: Odile Crane is the pen name of a former archivist of estate records in northern coastal towns, where sealed rooms and unclaimed inheritances were occupational hazards. She writes horror about houses that remember their families better than the families remember themselves.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Yara arrives at Ashgrove Hollow by night ferry, carrying his twin Ysolde's ashes and her unfinished letters. POV: Yara. He counts the doors out of habit—there is one more than he remembers. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into unease.

chapters.title: Lights No One Pays For
chapters.summary: Yara finds every lamp in the house burning despite the power being cut decades ago. The caretaker's ledger shows entries in Ysolde's handwriting dated after her death. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the first crack between what he knows and what the house insists.

chapters.title: A Face in the Hallway
chapters.summary: A portrait of a woman Yara doesn't recognize hangs in the east hall; the housekeeper, Mrs. Vell, calls her 'the last resident' and refuses to say more. POV: Yara. He notices the portrait's hands are freshly painted. Emotional beat: being watched by the house itself.

chapters.title: The Excavation Crew
chapters.summary: The crew digging the new well strikes something at forty feet—a door, oak and iron, sealed from the inside. The foreman, Brann, wants to leave it. POV: Brann. Emotional beat: professional dread overriding curiosity.

chapters.title: Counting Doors
chapters.summary: Ysolde's letters, read properly for the first time, describe a room Yara has never entered: a music room behind the cellar wall. POV: Yara. He finds the wall and it is warm. Emotional beat: his sister knew and never told him.

chapters.title: The Song in the Pipes
chapters.summary: At night the plumbing hums a lullaby Ysolde used to sing—half a melody, always stopping before the end. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into warning.

chapters.title: What the Casket Held
chapters.summary: Yara opens the urn early and finds not ash but river silt and a wedding ring belonging to the woman in the portrait. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the funeral he came to perform was never for his sister.

chapters.title: Mrs. Vell's Confession
chapters.summary: The housekeeper admits she has served the house for sixty years without aging a day since she stopped humming the song. POV: Mrs. Vell. Emotional beat: pity for a woman who traded memory for safety.

chapters.title: Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: Brann's crew breaches the door; inside is a music room, dustless, with a piano and sheet music in Ashgrove hands going back five generations. POV: Brann. Emotional beat: awe that feels like trespass.

chapters.title: The Verse That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Every score ends at the same bar line. The last verse exists only in singers' memories, and the last singer was Ysolde. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: inheritance as a debt with no paperwork.

chapters.title: The Portrait Ages Backward
chapters.summary: Yara compares an 1890s photograph to the portrait: the woman in the frame is younger now than in the photograph. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the house is spending something to keep her.

chapters.title: Ysolde's Room, Unchanged
chapters.summary: Yara finds his sister's room exactly as she left it at seventeen—except the sheets are warm and her half-finished diary gains a new line each night. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: love weaponized into a trap.

chapters.title: The Papers
chapters.summary: A solicitor's envelope appears on the hall table: deeds transferring Ashgrove Hollow to Yara, already signed by the last resident, awaiting only his name. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: a gift that reads like a summons.

chapters.title: Brann Won't Leave
chapters.summary: The foreman tries to pull his crew off the job; the road out floods overnight and the trucks won't start. POV: Brann. Emotional beat: a practical man confronting the impractical.

chapters.title: The First Verse
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vell teaches Yara the song's opening as it must be sung—eyes closed, hands flat on the piano, never alone in the room. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging.

chapters.title: What the House Buys
chapters.summary: Yara discovers the household's warmth, light, and Mrs. Vell's youth are drawn from the current singer, who ages in the resident's stead. Ysolde died of it. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: fury at an inheritance that eats its children.

chapters.title: The Resident Speaks
chapters.summary: The woman in the portrait speaks to Yara at midnight: her name is Lissandre Ashgrove, and she has been dying slowly since 1891, waiting for someone to sign and release her. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: compassion for the thing hunting him.

chapters.title: Ysolde's Half-Memory
chapters.summary: The diary's nightly lines turn out to be Ysolde writing through the house, offering fragments of the final verse—one bar per night, if Yara keeps singing the first. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: hope that costs exactly what he has.

chapters.title: The Crew Digs Deeper
chapters.summary: Compelled by the humming, Brann's crew excavates beneath the music room and finds older doors below—seven of them, each sealed from the inside, each with a name carved. POV: Brann. Emotional beat: the scale of the inheritance revealed.

chapters.title: Seven Singers
chapters.summary: Yara matches the carved names to the family Bible: every generation, one twin. The non-singing twin always buried the singer. He and Ysolde were never the exception—they were the pattern. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: identity collapsing into ritual.

chapters.title: Mrs. Vell Forgets
chapters.summary: The housekeeper begins losing decades at a time as Ysolde's death unbinds her bargain; she mistakes Yara for his grandfather and begs him not to sing. POV: Mrs. Vell. Emotional beat: horror of a mercy that was never mercy.

chapters.title: The Second Verse
chapters.summary: Ysolde's nightly fragment completes the second verse; singing it, Yara sees the house as it was—full, warm, alive—and understands what the residents gave up to keep it. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the trap's beauty made visible.

chapters.title: Brann's Name on a Door
chapters.summary: An eighth door is found, unsealed, with fresh carvings spelling BRANN. The foreman starts humming in his sleep. POV: Brann. Emotional beat: a man watching his own inheritance arrive.

chapters.title: Lissandre's Bargain
chapters.summary: The resident explains the papers: if Yara signs, she dies free and the house chooses a new resident from the singers; if he doesn't sign by the winter solstice, the house keeps him as singer and Ysolde's fragment dies with her. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: love against duty made explicit.

chapters.title: The Letters He Never Sent
chapters.summary: Yara finds the letters he wrote Ysolde as a child, returned unopened, stacked in the music room—she had been forbidden to know him. His grief turns toward the house itself. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: rage finding its true address.

chapters.title: The Third Verse Fails
chapters.summary: Yara sings the third verse alone and the house retaliates: doors multiply, the lights go out room by room, and something walks the halls wearing Ysolde's voice. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the cost of singing without witnesses.

chapters.title: What Was Sealed Inside
chapters.summary: Brann opens the innermost door and finds the first singer's remains at a piano, fingers on the keys, the final verse scored in her own blood—the only copy. POV: Brann. Emotional beat: revelation as desecration.

chapters.title: The Blood Score
chapters.summary: Yara copies the final verse but the notes rearrange when he looks away; the song will only hold for someone who learns it by heart, and heart is what it consumes. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: knowledge that cannot be safely possessed.

chapters.title: Mrs. Vell's Last Day
chapters.summary: The housekeeper remembers everything at once—every singer she watched die—and spends her final lucid hour teaching Yara how to sing without binding: as an elegy, not a contract. POV: Mrs. Vell. Emotional beat: a mentor's redemption at the end.

chapters.title: Ysolde's Voice in the Dark
chapters.summary: The thing wearing his sister's twin leads Yara to the well shaft and asks, in her exact voice, to be sung home. He nearly obeys. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief at its most dangerous.

chapters.title: The Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Roads clear for one day; Brann and the surviving crew flee, but Yara stays, unsigned, with the blood score and his sister's fragments. POV: Brann, departing. Emotional beat: the witness who chooses to remember rather than stay.

chapters.title: The Resident's Plea
chapters.summary: Lissandre shows Yara her true state—a century of stolen youth rotting beneath the paint—and begs him to sign, not for the house but so someone, finally, will bury her properly. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: pity completing the trap.

chapters.title: The Pen and the Piano
chapters.summary: Yara sits with the deed and the score through the longest night, understanding that signing and singing are the same act wearing different ink. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the stillness before decision.

chapters.title: He Signs His Sister's Name
chapters.summary: Yara signs the deed as YSOLDE ASHGROVE—releasing the resident to the sister who died mid-verse, letting the twins' shared inheritance settle on the one who already paid. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: love as forgery, duty as sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: With Lissandre free and the house unbound, Yara sings the complete final verse alone as an elegy—eyes open, hands off the keys—giving the song back its ending without giving it himself. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the climax; grief transmuted into release.

chapters.title: The House Goes Dark
chapters.summary: Lamp by lamp, Ashgrove Hollow goes out; the doors settle to their true number; the portrait crumbles to pigment and Ysolde's diary closes forever. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: an ending that feels like an exhale.

chapters.title: Burying Them Both
chapters.summary: Yara buries the silt, the ring, and the blood score in the frozen churchyard, carving one stone with two names. Mrs. Vell, old and mortal now, stands witness. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: mourning finally given its shape.

chapters.title: The Ferry in Thaw
chapters.summary: Yara leaves as the ice breaks; from the water he watches the Hollow stand dark and ordinary, visible for the first time to anyone passing. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the relief of being seen.

chapters.title: The Verse He Keeps
chapters.summary: Epilogue: months later, Yara teaches music in a coastal town and finds himself humming the song to quiet crying children—the melody, never the words. Some inheritances are just love with the contract torn out. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: peace with a residue.

chapters.title: A Door, Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: Final chapter: a new family moves into the Hollow; their daughter finds a small door behind the cellar wall, sealed from the inside, warm to the touch—and somewhere south, Yara wakes at midnight humming a verse he never learned. POV: the daughter, then Yara. Emotional beat: horror's long echo, and the choice to keep singing gently.
